comparison: Perfect alignment on hCG treatment effects (C107-C118). Both conclude that hCG stimulates androgen production but fails to restore normal Leydig cell differentiation markers, indicating missing factors in culture media.

Strong agreement on AR signaling dysfunction (C91-C99). Both accept findings of increased AR protein with impaired downstream signaling and altered target gene expression, though peer review acceptance is implicit within broader acknowledgment of molecular findings.

High concordance on steroid measurements (C79-C87, C89-C90). Both accept the paradoxical pattern of maintained testosterone despite reduced androstenedione and impaired enzyme expression, with peer reviewer explicitly noting responsiveness to gonadotrophin.

Agreement on steroidogenic enzyme downregulation (C69-C72, C74, C76). Both accept comprehensive evidence from multiple assays showing coordinated suppression of steroidogenic machinery as part of impaired steroidogenesis.

Partial overlap on steroidogenic defects. OpenEval R4 covers enzymes (C69-C78), while peer R1 addresses broader conclusions (C5-C9) and includes some enzyme claims (C69, C73, C75, C77, C78). Both find evidence compelling for steroidogenic impairment.

Agreement on estrogen pathway suppression (C100-C106). OpenEval notes paradoxical suppression despite elevated estradiol; peer review accepts these findings as part of compelling evidence for Leydig cell dysfunction.
Agreement on Leydig cell preservation and stress markers (C45-C48). Both accept quantitative findings showing maintained cell numbers with signs of stress and incomplete maturation at D16.
Partial agreement on Leydig cell maturation failure (C53-C55). Both accept evidence of incomplete maturation despite normal cell numbers, with peer review acknowledging tissue quality assessments.
Agreement on freeze-thaw comparison (C60-C63). Both accept that cryopreservation does not substantially alter Leydig cell characteristics, supporting clinical relevance of findings.

Partial overlap on differentiation markers (C49-C51). OpenEval addresses apoptosis and maturation markers; peer review accepts these as part of comprehensive molecular characterization showing impaired differentiation.
Minimal overlap on INSL3 and differentiation (C56). Both accept reduced adult markers as evidence of incomplete maturation, part of broader differentiation factor assessment.

Partial overlap on differentiation factors (C64-C67). OpenEval addresses gene expression in CSF vs FT comparison; peer review accepts these molecular findings as part of comprehensive characterization.

Agreement on main study conclusions (C5-C9). Both accept that culture system shows impaired Leydig cell differentiation and steroidogenesis requiring further optimization. Peer review finds evidence 'compelling.'

Agreement on mechanistic hypotheses (C125-C129). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN pending validation; peer review accepts these interpretations as useful for future optimization without challenging the proposed feedback mechanisms.

Agreement on steroid imbalance hypotheses (C120-C121). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN requiring experimental validation; peer review accepts these as reasonable mechanistic proposals aligned with missing factor interpretation.

Agreement on AR dysfunction interpretation (C124). OpenEval rates parallel to genetic models as UNCERTAIN; peer review implicitly accepts through acknowledgment of AR target gene data.
Agreement on cholesterol accumulation (C88-C90). Both accept selective free cholesterol increase as consistent with steroidogenic block rather than general cholesterol metabolism dysfunction.
